title: Proxy chaining to ZIA: setup, XFF handling and limits

what-it-is.statement: Proxy chaining forwards traffic from an existing on-premises proxy to the service with no other network change. Zscaler supports it but does not recommend it as a long-term production solution, because multiple proxies add latency and proxies that support failover support only manual failover.

quotes: Proxy chaining involves forwarding traffic from one proxy server to another.

Though Zscaler supports proxy chaining, it is not recommended as a long-term solution in production environments. Multiple proxies add latency and proxy servers that support failover support only manual failover.

registration.statement: The organization's public egress IP addresses must be registered with Zscaler Support (or the Zscaler representative during an evaluation); registration enforces IP uniqueness across organizations, and the gateway location is then defined in the Admin Console with those addresses.

quotes: This “registration” process enforces the uniqueness of IP addresses, so that an organization does not inadvertently use another organization’s IP addresses.
Ensure that your organization has been provisioned and send the IP address of your endpoint to Zscaler Support

primary-secondary.statement: The proxy must name both gateway.<cloud_name>.net and secondary.gateway.<cloud_name>.net as primary and secondary upstream servers; Zscaler does not support configurations with a single proxy server. The service then picks the nearest Public Service Edge by geolocation.

quotes: You must specify gateway.<cloud_name>.net and secondary.gateway.<cloud_name>.net as the primary and secondary proxy servers, respectively, to ensure fault tolerance. Zscaler does not support configurations with just one proxy server.
so the Zscaler service uses its Geolocation technology to forward the traffic to the nearest Public Service Edge

xff-handling.statement: When the service forwards a chained request onward it replaces the original X-Forwarded-For header with one holding the organization's public gateway IP, so internal addresses are not exposed; logs record the public IP of the sending firewall or router unless Internal IP Logging is enabled in Advanced Settings, which logs the XFF address.

quotes: it removes this original XFF header and replaces it with an XFF header that contains the IP address of the client gateway
you can go to the Advanced Settings page of the Zscaler Admin Console and enable Internal IP Logging.

limitations.statement: Chaining's stated limits: corporate-network users still need another method such as PAC files to reach the proxy, the proxy's latency adds to forwarding latency, and a caching proxy can cause downstream authentication problems and affect policy enforcement and reporting.

quotes: Users of the corporate network must use another method, such as PAC files, to forward traffic to the service.
The latency of the proxy server affects the traffic forwarding latency.
If the proxy server also performs caching, downstream authentication could be an issue.
If the local proxy has a cache, it could affect policy enforcement and reporting.

government-clouds.statement: Government clouds support proxy chaining only when the traffic from the on-premises proxy goes through a GRE or IPSec tunnel; chaining directly over the internet is not supported.

quotes: Zscaler Government Clouds support proxy chaining only when the proxy traffic forwarded from the on-premises proxy is sent through a GRE or IPSec tunnel.
